tools.name: get_big_trades
tools.description: Large aggressive orders ("big trades") from the trade tape of Binance, Bybit, OKX and Hyperliquid for a symbol. Answers: "Any whale market orders on BTC in the last hour?", "Were the big prints buying or selling?", "Which venue took the largest hit?". One big trade = all fills that share venue, taker side and exchange timestamp: a market order sweeping several price levels prints as many fills at one instant, and they are summed back into one trade. aggressor: buy = the taker bought, sell = the taker sold. Per trade: t = exchange timestamp, epoch ms; venue; price = volume-weighted fill price, USD; usd = notional, whole dollars. min_usd = smallest notional that counts, at least 50000; default = the asset's threshold on the MarketTrace chart (BTC and ETH 1000000; SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE and HYPE 500000; ZEC and ENA 100000); the response echoes the value used. totals = count (n) and summed usd of every trade at or above min_usd in the window, per side. trades = at most limit of them (1..=150, default 50): when there are more, the LARGEST are kept and truncated=true; the list is ordered by time. Window: from/to as RFC3339, YYYY-MM-DD or epoch ms; default the last hour; at most 12 h per call and from no older than 31 days, beyond either is an error, not a clamp. settled=false means the window reaches into the last 3 minutes, which the tape may not hold in full yet. coverage.venues lists the venues with tape in the window; an empty list means no tape there, not no trades (ZEC and ENA keep a 14-day tape). An order the trader split into separate child orders shows up as separate smaller trades. Descriptive: a big trade is executed flow, not a signal. Read-only.

from.description:
Window start: RFC3339, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC midnight) or epoch ms.
Default: `to` minus one hour. No older than 31 days.

limit.description: Trades listed, 1..=150 (default 50); the largest are kept.

min_usd.description:
Smallest notional that counts, whole USD, at least 50000. Default:
the asset's chart threshold (echoed in the response).

Read as any JSON value and checked in [`big_trades_query`], so a
fractional, negative or non-numeric value is an invalid_params NAMING
the parameter (a typed `u64` would fail inside rmcp's deserializer with
serde's "expected u64" and no field name). The schema says integer.

tools.name: get_conditional_outcomes
tools.description: Measured HISTORY of forward returns after a stated condition — the base rate from this feed's own data, replacing folklore like "high funding = squeeze". Answers: "What happened historically after funding above the 90th percentile?", "When OBI stayed bid-heavy while funding was positive, what did the next 24h look like?". Condition fields AND together (state at least one). Funding (multi-year series): funding_pct_gte/lte (AS-OF percentile 0..100 — the rank the live endpoint showed at that moment, no look-ahead), streak_h_gte (hours funding kept its sign), funding_sign (positive|negative). Archive (v2, 15-min state archive — YOUNG series, growing daily): archive_feature ∈ obi_skew (−1..+1) | oi_chg_1h_pct (%) | taker_buy_ratio (0..1) | basis_bps, with archive_gte/lte (raw value, no sample floor) and archive_pct_gte/lte (as-of percentile). An archive condition shrinks the match window to the INTERSECTION of the series' spans — the response window and coverage.archive.{window_days,n_samples} disclose exactly how thin the evidence is; weight accordingly. horizons: ["4h","24h","72h"] default, each 1h..168h. Per horizon: n_matches (raw), n_effective (overlap-collapsed — overlapping forward windows are NOT independent samples; all stats use the collapsed set), median/p10/p90 forward return in PERCENT, hit_rate_up (RATIO 0..1), max_dd_median_pct (median worst drawdown before the horizon resolves, ≤0). verdict=history_silent means the condition matched too rarely to measure (n_effective<12 on every horizon): a first-class answer — you are trading on belief, size accordingly; stats are null, never noise. warnings flag overlap collapse, 14-day clustering and silenced horizons. matches_sample = up to 50 audit timestamps. current = where the LAST hour of the same series sits on the condition axes (funding_pct as-of percentile, null below the floor; streak_h; sign) — read the band it falls in, then ask about that band; null only when there is no funding series. Percentile-form conditions exist only once the ranked series has coverage.warmup_samples (12) points — a STRUCTURAL floor (a rank among 2 points is degenerate), not a maturity gate; nothing time-based is withheld. Prices: Binance 1h closes (coverage.price_src). REPORTS HISTORY, NOT PREDICTIONS — past conditional distributions do not imply future returns. Read-only.

tools.name: get_footprint_events
tools.description: Order-book wall events from the 1-minute footprint of a symbol, built on the consolidated book and trade tape of Binance, Bybit, OKX and Hyperliquid. Answers: "Did a large resting order get absorbed on BTC in the last hour?", "Were bid walls pulled before this drop?", "How thin was the book this hour?". A wall = a resting price row far larger than the book's typical row (above median + 5 MAD of row sizes). kind=absorbed: trades hit the wall for at least 5% of its peak size, it still held at least 85% of that peak at the minute's close, and price did not break through it. kind=pulled: the wall fell below half of its peak while trades covered less than 30% of the drop, it did not refill within 2 seconds, and price had come within reach of it (cancelled, not filled). Scope: only price rows that traded in that minute and lie within the nearest 60 rows per side of mid are examined, so distant or untouched walls are not reported. wall_side: bid = resting buy orders, ask = resting sell orders. Per event: t = minute open, epoch ms; price = USD, lower edge of a `bucket`-wide row; peak_usd = largest resting size seen in the minute; executed_usd = volume traded against the wall; close_usd = resting size at the minute's close (whole dollars). At most 4 events of each kind are kept per minute, the largest peaks. thin_minutes = minutes whose resting depth near mid (within 25 bps, capped at the nearest 60 rows per side) was below the 20th percentile of the previous 2 hours, per side (bid, ask, both); classified = minutes of the window classified so far (the newest 2-3 minutes are still pending). Window: from/to as RFC3339, YYYY-MM-DD or epoch ms; default the last hour; at most 24 h per call, longer is an error, not a clamp. kinds = absorbed and/or pulled (default both); min_usd filters by peak_usd; limit 1..=150 (default 50) keeps the NEWEST events, counts cover the whole window and truncated=true says the list was cut. coverage.archive_from is when recording began; the archive only grows forward, so a window before it is honestly empty. Descriptive: an event states what the book did, not what price will do. Read-only.

midnight) or epoch milliseconds. Default: `to` minus one hour.

Events returned, 1..=150 (default 50). When the window holds more, the

min_usd.description: Smallest `peak_usd` that counts, USD, >= 0 (default 0 = every event).

Read-only.

tools.name: get_liquidations_recent
tools.description: Recent cross-exchange liquidation notional estimates for a symbol. Answers: "How much got liquidated on ETH in the last hour?", "Mostly longs or shorts?". Covers Binance, Bybit, OKX (not Hyperliquid). USD values are base quantity multiplied by each venue's source reference price; Bybit/OKX expose bankruptcy price, so these are estimates rather than execution notionals. Returns whole-dollar estimates, long_ratio (0..1 share of LONGS liquidated), notional_semantics, and event count for the window (window_s, default 3600, max 86400). Read-only.

Asset symbol: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE, HYPE, ZEC or ENA (case-insensitive; a
`USDT` suffix is accepted).

Look-back window in seconds, 1..=86400 (default 3600). Values beyond

Share of LONGS liquidated, RATIO 0..1 (0.71 = 71 % longs). `null` when
the window had zero notional.

n_events.description: Number of liquidation events in the window.

notional_semantics.description:
These are estimates (`base qty × source reference price`), not exchange-

tools.name: get_market_state
tools.description: Single normalized perpetual-futures microstructure snapshot for one crypto symbol, aggregated across Binance, Bybit, OKX and Hyperliquid. Answers: "What's the market state for BTC?", "Is ETH positioning stretched?". Covers BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE, HYPE, ZEC, ENA. Returns funding+2y-percentile, OI, volume, CVD aggression, order-book imbalance, recent liquidation pressure, basis, and key drivers. Scales: *_ratio fields are 0..1, percentiles are 0-100, rel.* are multipliers of the trailing median (1.4 = 140%), obi.skew is -1..+1 (positive = bid-heavy), cvd.delta_usd positive = net taker buying, basis_bps positive = perp above spot index. Every metric carries a coverage entry (venues, window depth, partial reason) — weight confidence by it. Read-only, ~30s fresh. Use first for market context; for the historical base rate of a condition you observe here (e.g. funding percentile ≥ 90), follow with get_conditional_outcomes. For volume-profile levels (POC, value area, naked POCs) use get_volume_profile; for large aggressive orders use get_big_trades. For absorbed or pulled order-book walls use get_footprint_events. For stacked buy or sell imbalances in the footprint use get_stacked_imbalances.

band sums past this cannot grow: equal bands mean "ran out of book",
not equal liquidity, bps.

VenueSlice.description:
One venue's slice of the cross-exchange picture — divergence across venues
is itself a signal the aggregates deliberately smooth away.

cvd_30m_usd.description: 30-min CVD, USD (positive = net taker buying on this venue).

funding_bps.description: Latest funding rate, 8h-normalized, bps (positive = longs pay shorts).

mid_div_bps.description: This venue's mid vs the consolidated mid, bps (positive = trades rich).

Venues.description:
Per-venue slices (fields null where a venue lacks the metric — e.g. no
Hyperliquid entry in a Binance-only series).

age_seconds.description: Worst-case age (seconds) across the live sources that fed the non-null live fields.

basis_bps.description:
Perp-vs-spot basis in bps: POSITIVE = perp trades ABOVE the spot
index ((mark − index) / index × 1e4).

drivers.description: Fact-strings for fields that have data; no verdict.

feed.description:
Server self-description: compare `feed.tools` with the tools you can
call — fewer on your side means a stale connector catalog (reconnect).

stale_venues.description: Venues currently degraded / dropped from consensus this cycle.

symbol.description: Uppercase asset symbol, e.g. `BTC`.

tools.name: get_ohlcv
tools.description: Consolidated cross-exchange OHLCV candles for a symbol (all four venues' trades merged onto one timeline). Answers: "Show me BTC 1h candles", "What's the 24h range?". Use for stop placement, position sizing (ATR), R:R and realized-volatility math — the exact-candle complement to get_market_state's approximate price block. Intervals: 5m, 15m, 1h, 4h, 1d (default 1h); limit 1..=200 candles (default 100), oldest first. The consolidated tape holds 31 days, so limit × interval must fit inside it: 1d ≤ 31, 4h ≤ 186, 1h and finer reach the full 200 — beyond that is an error, not a clamp. ZEC and ENA keep a 14-day tape that started filling when they were added, so their longer windows return fewer candles than asked — count what comes back. The NEWEST candle may be partial:true (bucket still forming) — exclude it from ATR/RV math. Fields: t = bucket open epoch ms, o/h/l/c = USD, v = traded volume in BASE units (BTC, ETH, ...), NOT USD — multiply by price for approximate notional. delta = taker-buy minus taker-sell volume inside the candle, BASE units like v (positive = net aggressive buying); the running sum of delta over the returned candles is the CVD of that window. Read-only.

symbol.description:
Asset symbol: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE, HYPE, ZEC or ENA (case-insensitive; a
`USDT` suffix is accepted).

Candle.description:
One OHLCV candle (consolidated cross-exchange trades, all four venues on
one timeline).

delta.description:
Taker-buy minus taker-sell volume in the bucket, BASE units like `v`
(positive = net aggressive buying). `null` when the upstream candle
carries no `delta` — never omitted.

partial.description:
`true` when the bucket is STILL FORMING (its close time is in the
future): o/h/l/c/v cover only part of the interval. EXCLUDE partial
candles from ATR/RV/average-volume math — a 1-minute-old hourly bar
otherwise crushes the last sample.

v.description: Traded volume in the bucket, BASE units (BTC, ETH, …) — NOT USD.

count.description: Number of candles returned (may be fewer than `limit` at history edges).

symbol.description: Uppercase symbol, e.g. `BTC`.

tools.name: get_stacked_imbalances
tools.description: Stacked imbalances in the footprint of a symbol, computed on the consolidated trade tape of Binance, Bybit, OKX and Hyperliquid. Answers: "Any stacked buying imbalance on BTC in the last hour?", "Where did aggressive selling stack up this morning?", "Which price bands saw one-sided market orders?". Rule (diagonal, the same as the MarketTrace footprint chart): each candle is split into price rows `bucket` wide; rows with no trades are skipped, so a row's neighbour is the nearest traded row above or below. A row is a buy imbalance when its taker-buy volume is at least ratio × the taker-sell volume of the nearest traded row below it, and a sell imbalance when its taker-sell volume is at least ratio × the taker-buy volume of the nearest traded row above it; a zero opposite side counts, zero against zero does not. A row counts only if its total volume is at least 10% of the candle's largest row. A stacked imbalance = 3 or more consecutive traded rows flagged on the same side within one candle; a row can sit in a buy run and a sell run at once. ratio = 2, 3 or 4 (default 3). interval = 1m, 5m, 15m or 1h candles (default 1m). Per event: t = candle open, epoch ms; kind = buy (aggressive buying) or sell (aggressive selling); low/high = USD band from the lower edge of the run's lowest row to the upper edge of its highest row (it may include untraded rows); rows = flagged rows in the run; usd = dominant-side volume of the run × row price, whole dollars; partial = true while the candle is still forming or closed less than 3 minutes ago (the tape may still add trades). candles = candles with trades in the window. counts = runs per kind in the whole window; events lists at most limit of them (1..=150, default 50): when there are more, the LARGEST by usd are kept and truncated=true; the list is ordered by time. kinds = buy and/or sell (default both). On BTC at ratio 3 a typical hour has about 38 runs on 1m candles, 13 on 5m, 4 on 15m and 1 on 1h. Window: from/to as RFC3339, YYYY-MM-DD or epoch ms; default the last hour; a candle is included when its open lies in [from, to); at most 12 h per call and from no older than 31 days, beyond either is an error, not a clamp. Rows are never merged: when zoomed out the chart merges rows and outlines fewer, wider runs, so it matches this output only at a zoom where each row is one bucket. coverage.venues lists the venues with tape in the window; an empty list means no tape there (ZEC and ENA keep a 14-day tape). Descriptive: an imbalance states where aggressive volume was one-sided, not what price will do. Read-only.

from.description:
Window start: RFC3339, `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC midnight) or epoch ms.
Default: `to` minus one hour. No older than 31 days.

limit.description: Runs listed, 1..=150 (default 50); the largest by usd are kept.

ratio.description:
Dominance ratio: 2, 3 or 4 (default 3).

Read as any JSON value and checked in [`stacked_imbalances_query`], so
2.5 or "3" is an invalid_params NAMING the parameter (a typed `u32`
would fail inside rmcp's deserializer with no field name). The schema
says integer.

symbol.description:
Asset symbol: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE, HYPE, ZEC or ENA (case-insensitive; a
`USDT` suffix is accepted).

to.description: Window end (exclusive), same formats. Default: now. At most 12 h after `from`.

CoverageEntry.description: Availability of a single metric group. `partial=false` + no `reason` means full data.

CoverageReason.description: Why a metric's `coverage` is `partial`. Absent/`null` when the metric is full.

oneOf.description: Compute exists (or will) but the trailing window is still filling.
Source or compute not deployed yet.
A venue in the set is unhealthy this cycle; metric on the reduced set.
The live source timestamp exceeds the freshness bound.

ImbalanceCounts.description: Runs per kind in the whole window, after `kinds` and before `limit`.

ImbalanceKind.description:
Which side's aggressive volume the run stacks on. Declared buy-first:
the response orders `buy` before `sell` at one candle.

oneOf.description: Taker-buy volume dominant (aggressive buying, the `ask` side).
Taker-sell volume dominant (aggressive selling, the `bid` side).

StackedImbalance.description:
One stacked imbalance: a run of 3+ consecutive traded rows of one candle
flagged on the same side.

high.description:
Upper edge of the run's highest row, USD (bucket decimals). The band
may include untraded rows, so `(high − low) / bucket` can exceed `rows`.

low.description: Lower edge of the run's lowest row, USD (bucket decimals).

partial.description:
`true` while the candle is still forming or closed less than 3
minutes ago (the tape may still add trades).

usd.description: Σ dominant-side volume × row price (lower edge) over the run, whole USD.

bucket.description: Price-row width of the symbol, USD (rows are never merged).

candles.description: Candles of the window with trades.

coverage.description:
`venues` = venues with at least one footprint cell in the window
(empty = no tape there).

events.description:
At most `limit` runs — the largest by `usd` — ordered by `t`, then
`kind` (buy first), then `low`.

from.description: Window start as given (inclusive), RFC3339 UTC.

symbol.description: Uppercase asset symbol, e.g. `BTC`.

to.description: Window end as given (exclusive), RFC3339 UTC.

truncated.description: `true` when the window held more runs than `limit`.

tools.name: get_state_history
tools.description: Time series of any numeric market-state fields from the 15-minute full-state archive — the derivative/trend view get_market_state cannot give. Answers: "How did OI build over the last 3 days?", "Is funding percentile rising or falling this week?", "When did the book skew flip?". fields = dotted numeric paths of get_market_state (1..=16), e.g. funding.percentile, oi.usd, obi.skew, cvd.delta_usd, basis_bps, price.last, depth.bid_usd.10bps, venues.binance.oi_usd. Returns parallel arrays: t (epoch ms, ascending) + series[field] aligned with t; null = that field was not populated in the archived row (honest hole, common near the archive's start — blocks accrue at their own pace). Downsampling: max_points 1..=1000 (default 200); stride in the response says how many 15-min rows each point skips; the newest row is never sampled away. coverage.archive_from/to are the WHOLE archive's bounds — the archive is YOUNG (born 2026-07-03) and grows a row per 15 min per asset; a thin answer is honest, not broken. from/to accept RFC3339, YYYY-MM-DD or epoch ms. Read-only.

fields.description:
Dotted numeric paths of the market state, 1..=16 per request — e.g.
`funding.percentile`, `oi.usd`, `obi.skew`, `cvd.delta_usd`,
`basis_bps`, `price.last`, `depth.bid_usd.10bps`,
`venues.binance.oi_usd`. Typos get an error naming the offender.

from.description:
Range start: RFC3339 (`2026-07-03T08:00:00Z`), `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC
midnight), or epoch milliseconds. Default: the whole archive.

max_points.description:
Points returned after downsampling, 1..=1000 (default 200). The
response's `stride` says how many archived rows each point skips.

symbol.description:
Asset symbol: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE, HYPE, ZEC or ENA (case-insensitive; a
`USDT` suffix is accepted).

to.description: Range end, same formats. Default: the whole archive.

HistoryCoverage.description: Provenance of the archive behind a history answer.

archive_from.description:
First archived tick, RFC3339 UTC — `null` only while the archive is
completely empty.

step_minutes_nominal.description: Writer cadence between rows, minutes (15; holes possible).

from.description: First returned point, RFC3339 UTC (empty string when no points).

n_available.description: Rows available in the requested range BEFORE downsampling.

series.description: Requested dotted field → one value per point (aligned with `t`).

stride.description: Downsampling stride actually applied (1 = every archived row).

symbol.description: Uppercase asset symbol, e.g. `BTC`.

t.description: Epoch-ms per returned point, ascending (ms like `get_ohlcv`'s `t`).

to.description: Last returned point, RFC3339 UTC (empty string when no points).

tools.name: get_volume_profile
tools.description: Volume-profile reference levels for a symbol, from the consolidated trade tape of Binance, Bybit, OKX and Hyperliquid. Answers: "Where are the key volume levels on BTC?", "Is price inside yesterday's value area?", "Any untested POCs nearby?". Sessions are UTC days. poc = price row with the most traded volume; vah/val = top and bottom of the value area, the band around the POC that holds 70% of the session's volume. Returns today (the session still forming, developing:true, its levels still move), days (the last N complete days, days 1..=30, default 7, oldest first), composite (one profile over those days plus today) and naked_pocs (POCs of the last 30 complete days that price has not traded back to since). Per profile: poc/vah/val in USD (lower edge of a `bucket`-wide price row), va_width_pct = (vah − val) / poc × 100, volume in BASE units (BTC, ETH, ...), taker_buy_ratio 0..1 (share of volume that was aggressive buying). va_width_rank.percentile (0-100) ranks the latest complete day's va_width_pct among the last n_days complete days: low = an unusually tight day; null below 12 days. Levels only, no histogram. For where price sits against these levels read price.last from get_market_state. ZEC and ENA were added later, so fewer days come back for them: count what is returned and read coverage. Read-only.

days.description:
Complete UTC days to return, 1..=30 (default 7). Out of range is an
error, not a clamp.

symbol.description:
Asset symbol: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB, XRP, DOGE, HYPE, ZEC or ENA (case-insensitive; a
`USDT` suffix is accepted).

CompositeProfile.description: One profile over the returned complete days plus today (when present).

from.description: First day inside the composite, `YYYY-MM-DD` (`null` when empty).

includes_today.description: Whether today's developing session is summed in.

to.description: Last day inside the composite (today's date when it includes today).

CoverageEntry.description: Availability of a single metric group. `partial=false` + no `reason` means full data.

CoverageReason.description: Why a metric's `coverage` is `partial`. Absent/`null` when the metric is full.

oneOf.description: Compute exists (or will) but the trailing window is still filling.
Source or compute not deployed yet.
A venue in the set is unhealthy this cycle; metric on the reduced set.
The live source timestamp exceeds the freshness bound.

poc.description:
Point of control: the price row with the most traded volume, USD
(lowest price on a tie).

taker_buy_ratio.description: Share of the volume that was aggressive buying (taker bought), 0..1.

vah.description:
Value-area high: top row of the band around the POC holding 70% of the
day's volume, USD.

val.description: Value-area low: bottom row of that band, USD.

volume.description: Traded volume, BASE units (BTC, ETH, …), not USD.

NakedPoc.description: A complete day's POC that no later day (today included) has traded through.

date.description: The day whose POC it is, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

price.description: USD, lower edge of the `bucket`-wide row.

TodayProfile.description: Today's session, still forming: its levels move until 00:00 UTC.

developing.description: Always `true`: the session is not complete.

VaWidthRank.description:
Where the latest complete day's `va_width_pct` ranks among the complete
days of the last 60 (itself included).

n_days.description: Sample size the rank was taken in.

percentile.description: 0-100; low = an unusually tight day. `null` below 12 days.

days.description:
`window_days` = complete days returned; `partial` + `accruing` when
fewer than asked.

today.description: `partial` + `stale` when today's session could not be served.

as_of.description:
Coverage time of today's session, RFC3339 UTC (build time when today
is `null`).

days.description: The last N complete UTC days that have data, oldest first.

naked_lookback_days.description: Complete days actually checked for naked POCs (≤ 30).

symbol.description: Uppercase asset symbol, e.g. `BTC`.

today.description: Today's developing session; `null` when it could not be served.
